question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-1.5<X<1.5)=0.3472,$ use the table to find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6331\,$ | $\,0.6368\,$ | $\,0.6406\,$ |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6700\,$ | $\,0.6736\,$ | $\,0.6772\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7054\,$ | $\,0.7088\,$ | $\,0.7123\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.5<X<1.5) & =0.3472 \\ 2P(0<X<1.5) & =0.3472 \\ P(0<X<1.5) & =0.1736 \\ P(X<1.5)-P(X<0) & =0.1736 \\ P(X<1.5)-0.5 & =0.1736 \\ P(X<1.5) & =0.6736 \\ P(X\le 1.5) & =0.6736\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1.5) & =0.6736 \\ P(Z\le \frac{1.5-0}{\sigma }) & =0.6736 \\ Φ(\frac{1.5}{\sigma }) & =0.6736 \\ \frac{1.5}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.6736)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.45)=0.6736\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.6736)=0.45.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1.5}{\sigma } & =0.45 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{1.5}{0.45} \\ \sigma  & ≈3.33\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
